capabilities: Open EPUB, MOBI, AZW3, FB2 and CBZ files stored in the vault
Annotate passages with marks, notes and bookmarks
Read books aloud with on-device text-to-speech
Download books from Project Gutenberg and OPDS catalogs
Export books and annotations to PDF, Markdown or EPUB
extras: Interface is English only and has not been tested with screen readers; no accounts, ads or telemetry, book files are never modified, and reading data is kept as plain JSON in a !orbis-data folder beside each book.
motivation: The author wanted reading to be part of the user's knowledge base, on the user's own terms.
problem: Obsidian cannot open or read ebooks, so books and the annotations made in them sit outside the vault and outside the note system.

relations.evidence: The open-source projects Orbis Reader builds on, such as foliate-js and lamejs
Browse, search and download books from Project Gutenberg (built in), your own Calibre server and other OPDS-compatible sources

summary: Ebook reader that opens EPUB, MOBI, AZW3, FB2 and CBZ files in the vault, with annotation, on-device text-to-speech, a note-based library and export.
